audit.whatIsWrong: First item and two items both read Jayce, while whys[5] and whys[6] on the same page say Seraph's flips the lane and that two-item Ryze outpaces his scaling entirely.
audit.why: Packet chart and the audited Jayce-side mirror both give Ryze the last two stages.
audit.corrected: First item and 2+ items flipped to Ryze with ratings, as matched full+content pairs.

audit.why: Level 2 with Acceleration Gate into Shock Blast is his laning peak, Level 6 is macro-only for Ryze (Realm Warp is a delayed group portal), and Seraph's is the flip — the spikes[] already say this and now the chart agrees.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says four times that Ryze needs melee range, and calls Shock Blast 'point-and-click'.
audit.why: Overload is 1000 range and Spell Flux 615 — Ryze never enters melee, and at level 1 he actually out-reaches Shock Blast's 600. Shock Blast is a fired orb that detonates on the first enemy hit, so a minion body-blocks it; that is the counterplay the page omits. Rune Prison only roots through Spell Flux. The weapon swap is a 6-second auto-attack reset whose first cannon-form hit reduces armour and MR — that is why his opening burst lands so hard, and the wind-up is the step-back tell.
audit.corrected: Real ranges substituted for 'melee range', Shock Blast restated as a blockable skillshot, and the swap named as the burst tell.

audit.why: suspectNames flagged 'Realm Warps' in whys[6] — false positive, that is Ryze's own R as a verb.

edits.before: Gate-accelerated poke — stand behind minions and close after it whiffs. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Shock Blast is a skillshot orb — body-block it with a minion, then close while it is down and he is stuck in cannon.

edits.before: Track Jayce’s Shock Blast: Gate-accelerated poke — stand behind minions and close after it whiffs. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Shock Blast: a skillshot, and a minion body-blocks it. His first hit after swapping to cannon shreds your armour and MR.

edits.before: That is Jayce’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: The weapon swap is a 6s auto reset — the wind-up is your cue to step back.

edits.before: Both champions have only a single damaging spell at level 1, but Jayce's Shock Blast fires safely from cannon range while your Q demands melee proximity — pure Skill, and one you're likely to lose if you test it.
edits.after: Both have one damaging spell at level 1, and Overload's 1000 range out-reaches Shock Blast's 600 — but his skillshot hits far harder, so it stays a read, and one you lose if you stand still to test it.

edits.before: With hammer-stance Thundering Blow knockback added at level 3, Jayce can interrupt any melee engage you attempt; your Flux loop needs sustained melee range and he denies exactly that.
edits.after: With Thundering Blow's knockback added at level 3, Jayce shoves you straight out of your own 615-range Spell Flux window, and the loop needs you holding that range to work at all.

edits.before: Jayce swaps to hammer stance to push you under tower and denies your Flux combo; without melee range you cannot E-Q-W cycle at all.
edits.after: Jayce swaps to hammer stance to shove you under tower; pinned there you never get inside 615 to start the E-Q-W cycle at all.

edits.before: Swap to hammer stance to shove the wave and shove you under tower, killing the melee-range Flux cycling your pattern demands
edits.after: Swap to hammer stance to shove the wave and pin you under tower, outside the 615-range window your Flux cycle demands

edits.before: At level 1 you have only Q and must walk into melee range to trade — Jayce punishes this instantly with a point-and-click Shock Blast through his Acceleration Gate before your W root even exists. Hug the edge of XP range, last-hit with Q at max distance, and do not step past your minions. At level 2 your W root gives you a threat, but Jayce's empowered Q still fires from full cannon range and deletes more HP than your W-Q combo returns — the trade is still negative. Level 3 completes your E-W-Q loop but only matters if Jayce is already in melee range, which he will never willingly be. Spend early game banking Manaflow stacks and Tear charges; the goal is to reach first back with Tear and enough gold for Seraph's components, not to win the 1v1.
edits.after: At level 1 you have only Q, but it reaches 1000 to his 600 — the danger is not his range, it is that Shock Blast through an Acceleration Gate hits far harder than anything you have. Hug the edge of XP range, last-hit at max distance, and keep a minion between you and the orb; it detonates on the first thing it touches. At level 2 your W gives you a threat, but it only roots through Spell Flux and his gated Q still deletes more HP than your W-Q returns — the trade is negative. Level 3 completes the E-W-Q loop, but it needs him inside 615, which he will never willingly be. Bank Manaflow stacks and Tear charges; the goal is a first back with Tear, not a 1v1 win.

notes: Two corrections worth flagging. The page repeatedly told the player Ryze must walk into melee range — Overload is 1000 and Spell Flux 615, and at level 1 Ryze actually out-reaches Shock Blast's 600, so the reason to respect Jayce is his damage, not his range. And Shock Blast was called point-and-click; it is a fired orb that detonates on the first enemy hit, which means a minion body-blocks it — the single most useful piece of counterplay in the matchup and it was absent. Chart's last two rows flipped to Ryze per the packet and the audited mirror; the content whys[5]/[6] already argued for it.
